analysis:
This batch contains only test code; I found no security regression in it. ClusterApprovalFixture.swift head 310-327 adds ClusterApprovalMacs.startedLeaderService. It is a refactor of the helper removed from ClusterServiceRestartingStopTests.swift (base 32-44, head 32), and the behavior is the same: a dry-run wizard, /usr/bin/true as the executable, and a leadership record marked serving.

ClusterOnboardingStopsAskedTests.swift (new, head 1-85) exercises new production behavior. It covers the ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked and ClusterControlRequest.stopsBefore wire fields and decoding of replies from older peers. It also covers OnboardingLive.recordStop(asked:), localStop(asked:), localServe(unlessStoppedSince:), currentStopsAsked and followerStatus. The tests check that a start never undoes a stop a person asked for since the start began.

The production implementations (OnboardingLive, ClusterService, the ClusterControlReply/ClusterControlRequest types) are not in this batch. Integration should check them:
- Whether a paired peer, which may be adversarial, can make a stop look requested or suppress one by sending a forged stopsAsked/stopsBefore value. This is availability only; the closest canonical concerns are A-018 and TB-012/T-059/T-060.
- Whether a missing count from an older Mac fails toward serving, as the test at line 33 expects.
- Whether stopsAsked decoding is bounded and overflow-safe.

None of this touches attestation, encryption, the prompt path (A-001) or the cache (T-041). No threat-model update is needed from these tests alone.
